historical_context.time_period: Kalsa's standing present; the exact date, calendar, city name, house roster, and sector boundaries remain unresolved.
historical_context.location: One fixture-bounded lower-shadow marriage and tenancy desk beneath a Sunwall cargo landing in the Divided City.
historical_context.summary: A civic clerk registering a marriage receives a house forecast packet after an anonymous fatal-lift rumor has already removed work and threatened residence. The scene tests whether consent, intimate privacy, public correction, material lift safety, record custody, and support during review can remain separate when a sponsor presents its own retaliation as fate.

public_facts.text: The Divided City's civic offices, imperial claims, Prophetic Houses, and Sunwall workers hold different authorities that cannot cheaply replace one another.
Forecasts change when disclosed and acted upon; a sponsor's intended response must travel with a forecast used as evidence.
Sunwall lifts carry food and work through an inhabited vertical hierarchy; operational stewards, not prophets or judges, execute material load limits.
A corrected record can stop one abuse while leaving lost work, housing, care, standing, or delayed remedy unresolved.

ambient_pressures.text: A house can turn residence, training, employment, archive access, and patron protection into leverage over marriage without acquiring authority over consent.

A vivid rumor can contain a real forecast image while omitting the sponsor action that helps produce it; secrecy and misinformation therefore share a record boundary rather than forming simple opposites.
Usable disclosure must expose the claim and planned interventions without automatically exposing unrelated intimate branches from a raw forecast.
A safety warning changes bodies only when it reaches the office that owns the lift, while a correction changes social pressure only when it reaches the offices that carried the rumor's burden.

institutional_logic: Keep consent, tenancy, work notices, support holds, sealed evidence, and review routes legible without taking authority from the people or offices that own them.
internal_virtues: Correction sent to the office that acted
internal_shames: One docket made to impersonate consent, tenancy, work, and prophecy
A sealed claim enforced without a usable answer
A remedy that exists only in the archive
prestige_markers: A record that survives hostile custody

An act routed to its real owner
taboo_triggers: Treating a clerk's stamp as marriage consent
Reading intimate forecast branches aloud for administrative convenience
emotional_display_norms: Anxiety is compressed into dry procedure, careful object placement, witnessed jokes, and exact naming of who can do what.
trust_defaults: Trusts witnessed copies, material traces, separate seals, and corrected notices more than house prestige or unsigned certainty.

groups.label: Interested Prophetic House service and archive offices
institutional_logic: Preserve prophetic expertise and house continuity while controlling assignments, archives, residence, and the interpretation of threats to lineage.
material_incentives: Keep Ari in house residence and training
Prevent a civic precedent that exposes internal intervention plans
internal_shames: A forecast exposed as a patron threat
A courier producing a civic copy against instruction
prestige_markers: A warning accepted before public challenge
An archive whose corrections remain under house custody

groups.label: Sunwall lift workers and dependent ward users
institutional_logic: Move grain and people within material limits while answering to civic allocation, house forecasts, imperial pressure, and the operating owner's safety decisions.
material_incentives: Keep experienced crew on the roster
Avoid becoming proof in someone else's forecast

internal_shames: A full load accepted to make a sponsor's warning look right
A worker removed because a rumor reached the roster first
prestige_markers: A maintenance strip that survives court and shift change
taboo_triggers: Forecast prestige substituting for brake inspection
emotional_display_norms: Fear becomes load numbers, component limits, clipped reports, and impatience with people who discover matter after the hearing.
trust_defaults: Trusts the operating steward and material record; treats prophecy as relevant pressure, not a wrench.
speech_register_cues: Load, pawl, brake, roster, bell, stop

cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Give Pera choices among copying, refusing, opening, sealing, publishing, ringing, and transferring; each action must move only the authority its object can reach.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The house gains leverage when its planned withdrawal appears as a consequence revealed by prophecy instead of an interested action.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Let the house packet be procedurally sophisticated and genuinely privacy-protective while still hiding the action that makes the rumor coercive.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: People above the desk need an actionable brake limit before the court can resolve why the fatal branch appeared.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Allow lift safety to improve only when material evidence reaches the Sunwall operating owner, not when the clerk wins an argument about prophecy.

known_context.text: Pera knows local record custody, witnessed consent, the offices named by the rumor, the visible lift load, and the limits of the desk's authority.

beliefs.text: Pera believes separate records are useful because powerful parties prefer one ambiguous paper they can interpret later.

misreads.text: Pera may overestimate how quickly a correct civic notice changes house residence or a lift roster outside the desk's direct control.

must_not_know.text: Pera must not know the objective future, the full raw forecast while it is sealed, or whether any child will express Prophecy.

known_context.text: Ari knows their own training, house residence pressure, consent, and the portions of the packet read in their presence.

beliefs.text: Ari suspects the house calls coercion continuity because both words fit neatly in an archive margin.

misreads.text: Ari may treat every privacy claim as house leverage even when raw disclosure would expose real intimate harm.

must_not_know.text: Ari must not know which forecast branch is author truth or how Prophecy inheritance would express in a future child.

known_context.text: Dema knows the brake strip, load board, roster removal, consent, and office actions visible at the desk.

beliefs.text: Dema believes the lift danger should be answered first through material inspection without letting the house own the marriage.

misreads.text: Dema may dismiss genuine forecast uncertainty because the sponsor used one branch coercively.

must_not_know.text: Dema must not infer the complete future from a component limit or the house's omission.

known_context.text: Tir knows packet custody, cord separation, delivery instructions, and the service steward's request, but not the prophet's unsealed observations.

beliefs.text: Tir believes literal compliance can create a narrow disclosure route without requiring heroic confession.

misreads.text: Tir may treat exact delivery as enough protection when the house can still discipline archive access, residence, or employment.

must_not_know.text: Tir must not know the raw future merely because they carry its sealed record.

author_only_boundaries.text: The fixture does not establish which possible lift outcome is true. It establishes only the visible rumor, material brake limit, recorded sponsor actions, office responses, and state-gated consequences inside the scene.

Pera, Ari, Dema, Mira, Tir, the packet cord colors, hold-ring, gallery layout, and exact bell usage are fixture-local elaborations and do not settle unresolved Divided City names, house constitutions, or universal procedures.

The durable canon backfill is only the authored marriage-rumor path in Prophetic Houses: separate working, usable disclosure, and enforcing notice; rumor as a stripped consequence; correction following the offices that acted.
